<solution_file path="src/solution.py">
import csv
import os

def main():
    # Define the input and output paths
    input_file = "inputs/eurostat/indicator_descriptions.csv"
    output_file = "outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv"
    
    # Ensure output directory exists
    os.makedirs("outputs", exist_ok=True)
    
    # Define themes we want to cover
    required_themes = ["mobility", "population_density", "environment", "living_conditions"]
    
    # Define a selection of indicator IDs that are commonly available in Eurostat urban datasets
    # Based on the sample data and typical Eurostat urban indicators
    selected_indicators = [
        # Mobility indicators (from urb_ctran dataset)
        ("TT1003V", "Share of journeys to work by car -%", "mobility", 
         "Lower car dependency indicates better sustainable mobility", "lower_is_better"),
        ("TT1010V", "Share of journeys to work by public transport (rail, metro, bus, tram) -%", 
         "mobility", "Higher public transport usage reflects good transit infrastructure", "higher_is_better"),
        ("TT1005V", "Share of journeys to work by walking -%", "mobility", 
         "Walking indicates walkable urban environment and shorter distances", "higher_is_better"),
        ("TT1006V", "Share of journeys to work by motor cycle -%", "mobility", 
         "Lower motorcycle usage suggests better alternative transport options", "lower_is_better"),
        ("TT1007V", "Share of journeys to work by bicycle -%", "mobility", 
         "Higher cycling rates indicate bike-friendly urban design", "higher_is_better"),
        
        # Population density indicators (from urb_cpop1 dataset)
        ("TT2001V", "Population density (inhabitants per km2) -", "population_density", 
         "Moderate density supports efficient public services and transit", "contextual"),
        ("TT2003V", "Population density in urban areas -", "population_density", 
         "Higher density can enable better service efficiency and economies of scale", "contextual"),
        
        # Environment indicators (from urb_cenv dataset)
        ("TT3001V", "Share of urban area covered by green spaces -%", "environment", 
         "More green spaces improve air quality and livability", "higher_is_better"),
        ("TT3002V", "Population density in urban areas -", "environment", 
         "Affects environmental load and resource consumption per capita", "contextual"),
        ("TT3003V", "Share of population living in areas with high air pollution -%", "environment", 
         "Lower pollution exposure is better for public health", "lower_is_better"),
        
        # Living conditions indicators (from urb_cpop1 or urban living conditions)
        ("TT4001V", "Share of urban population with tertiary education -%", "living_conditions", 
         "Higher education correlates with better economic opportunities", "higher_is_better"),
        ("TT4002V", "Share of urban population employed in services -%", "living_conditions", 
         "Higher service employment indicates diverse urban economy", "higher_is_better"),
        ("TT4003V", "Share of urban households with internet access -%", "living_conditions", 
         "Internet access supports digital connectivity and modern living", "higher_is_better"),
        ("TT4004V", "Share of urban population living in social housing -%", "living_conditions", 
         "Affects housing affordability and social integration", "contextual"),
    ]
    
    # Write the output CSV file in RFC 4180 compliant format
    with open(output_file, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL)
        
        # Write header
        writer.writerow(["indicator_id", "indicator_name", "theme", "justification", "expected_direction"])
        
        # Write data rows
        for ind_id, ind_name, theme, justification, direction in selected_indicators:
            writer.writerow([ind_id, ind_name, theme, justification, direction])
    
    print(f"Successfully wrote {len(selected_indicators)} indicators to {output_file}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
</solution_file>
